company_name: China Merchants Port Holdings Company Limited
model: Sum-of-parts: owner-FCF DCF of consolidated port operations plus equity-accounted associates and JVs valued separately in the equity bridge (listed at market, unlisted at an earnings multiple)

inputs.share_count_basis: 4,198,009,186 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, MD&A 'Share capital and financial resources'); no options, convertibles or share awards, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT. The count rose 3,278m -> 4,198m over FY2017-FY2023 through scrip-dividend elections; no scrip issuance since 2024. Renewed scrip elections would be non-SBC dilution and are flagged as a risk, not modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: None: CMPort operates no share option or share award scheme and the FY2025 annual report carries only HKFRS 2 boilerplate (0144.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:4570), no share-based payment expense. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (HKEX, Friday); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are HKD-reported (USD peg) but earned mostly in RMB plus BRL/LKR/XOF/TRY frontier markets. Cost of equity 9.2% = HKD/USD risk-free 4.0% + beta 0.8 x 6.5% ERP (China/EM blended, including country premium for Sri Lanka, Brazil, West Africa). After-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (FY2025 finance costs 1,506 on ~HK$34bn average borrowings = 4.4%, largely non-deductible at the HK holdco). Market weights: equity HK$72bn vs net debt HK$20bn (D/V ~22%) -> WACC ~8.0%. Same rate in every scenario; scenario risk lives in the flows. Associates are valued outside the DCF (listed at market, unlisted at a P/E), so the WACC applies only to consolidated operations.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (1,413 non-current + 98 current = 1,511 at 30 Jun 2026) and the TCP Brazil concession liabilities (2,865 non-current + 96 current = 2,961 at 31 Dec 2025, FY2025 AR note 32) are deducted once in the equity bridge; the 'repayment of lease liabilities, concession liabilities and royalty provision' line (466 FY2025) is NOT deducted from flows. total_debt is bank and other borrowings only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. Flows are 100%-consolidated subsidiary flows; NCI (Hambantota 85%, TCP 90%, Shenzhen western ports, Zhanjiang etc.) takes ~28% of consolidated subsidiary profit (FY2025 NCI 1,184 vs ~4.1bn subsidiary profit after tax; segment note 5). NCI is deducted at 28% of the base-case consolidated-operations EV rather than at its 17,282 book value, because the operating subsidiaries are worth well above book. Perpetual capital securities were fully redeemed in 2025 (nil at 30 Jun 2026).
inputs.associates_treatment: Equity-accounted associates and JVs (~55% of FY2025 profit before tax; share of profit 4,970 vs consolidated EBIT 5,276) are NOT in the flows: the 2,730 of associate/JV dividends sitting inside reported OCF is removed from the FCF base (last_fcf 5,869 = reported OCF 9,472 - associate dividends 2,730 - capex 873). Instead the stakes enter the bridge: SIPG (28.06%, the one material associate) at market, other listed associates at their 31-Dec-25 disclosed market value, and unlisted associates + JVs at 12x normalised share of profit. Discounting associate dividends at the group WACC would mismatch an equity flow with an unlevered rate, and SIPG retains ~70% of earnings so a dividend capitalisation would value the stake at half its quoted price.
inputs.notes: MODEL: routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' -> owner-FCF DCF + adaptations (currency, leases, NCI, non-operating assets/excluded income, SBC-zero), straddled with a holdco-style sum-of-parts because ~half of economic profit is equity-accounted. No prior valuation and no MEMORY.md entry: this is a fresh build. FCF BASE: reported FCF 8,599 (OCF 9,472 - capex 873) includes 2,730 associate dividends; interest paid sits in financing and interest received in investing, so the remaining 5,869 is an unlevered consolidated-operations flow with no interest income to strip. FY2025 capex (6.5% of revenue) is a five-year low; the forward path uses ~10% (FY2021-25 average 11.0%; H1 FY2026 accrual capex 691 vs 404 cash). EBITDA: not reported at group level on the statutory face; derived as gross profit + other income - admin + D&A = 7,561 (56.6%) FY2025, 7,456 (55.8%) ex the 105 of other gains; H1 FY2026 58.9%, H1 FY2025 59.7% (management's segment EBITDA, pre-corporate costs, 63.1% in H1 FY2026). CASH TAX: FY2025 tax paid 1,112 incl. 191 withholding on associate dividends; ~730 on ~5.3bn subsidiary EBIT = 13.8%, H1 FY2026 higher; path 18% -> 20% (PRC 25% statutory, Brazil 34%, Sri Lanka concessions). BUYBACKS: none ever; flat count is a convention the company does not fund. SBC-zero: band_position null.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote both HKD; no conversion on the headline. The SIPG stake is marked in RMB: 600018.SS RMB 5.50 close 2026-10-09 x ~6,533m shares (28.06% of 23,284m) x CNYHKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10) = HK$42,117m; ties to the company's own 31-Dec-25 disclosure of HK$39,193m (note 20(a)) given the RMB appreciation and the share-price move since.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.7% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr 8.3% and EPS 5yr 1.0%. Revenue has been lifted by acquisitions and consolidations (and FX) while attributable EPS has been flat-to-down because associate profits (SIPG) fell 23.7% in FY2025 and the share count rose ~28% via scrip dividends FY2017-23. EPS CAGRs are per-share and absorb that dilution.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on reported OCF - capex (SBC is zero, interest sits outside OCF, so owner FCF = reported); they include associate dividends and FY2020's low base, and flatter the trend. FY2025 FCF also benefits from five-year-low capex. Base FY2017-FY2025 annual series from 0144.HK_Metrics.csv.

base.narrative: H1 FY2026 revenue +13% carries FY2026 to ~+10%, then growth fades to volume-plus-tariff inflation as the frontier terminals' ramp matures. Margin held at the FY2025/H1 FY2026 midpoint; capex normalised to ~10% of revenue.
base.terminal_cap_note: 12x FCF (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x): port concessions are finite (TCP Brazil to 2048, PRC land-use rights ~50 years, Hambantota 99-year lease), so a perpetual-renewal multiple is not granted. First build used 14/15/12 and implied 1.05x book and ~17x TTM earnings against a FY2017-25 range of 0.39-0.92x and ~5-11x; caps lowered before shipping.

scenario_narratives.base: China container volumes grow low-single-digit, the frontier terminals (Hambantota +80% in FY2025, Djibouti, Lomé, Indonesia NPH) keep adding throughput but at a slowing rate, and TCP Brazil holds share. Consolidated revenue +10% in FY2026 on the H1 run-rate, fading to ~2.5% by year 9. EBITDA margin ~57%, capex ~10% of revenue. Associates are carried at today's market price for SIPG and ~12x normalised earnings for the rest, i.e. no recovery or further decline is assumed in the associate book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Belt-and-Road trade keeps outgrowing China's overall trade (51.9% share in 2025), the frontier concessions ramp to utilisation with operating leverage (margin to 60%), and container-tariff pressure from fleet oversupply proves short-lived. Growth 12% in FY2026 and 4-7% for five years. Associate upside (SIPG profit recovering from the FY2025 -22% drop, Terminal Link) is NOT in the flows; it would add roughly HK$1 per share for every 10% re-rating of the associate stakes.
scenario_narratives.bear: US-China tariff escalation and carrier-alliance reshuffles (KMCT Kaohsiung -25% on route changes) cut transshipment and gateway volumes, China property weakness keeps bulk cargo falling, and a frontier-market concession event (Sri Lanka sovereign stress, Red Sea/Horn of Africa disruption, Nigeria/Togo) impairs an overseas terminal. Revenue flat after FY2026, margin compresses to 53%, capex stays heavier at 11%, cash tax rises to 22%. Associate values are held at market in all scenarios, so a further SIPG de-rating is an additional unmodelled downside of ~HK$1 per share per 10%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because the business is exposed to tariff-driven trade-flow shocks and to frontier-market concession risk that can impair a terminal with little warning. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both sustained frontier ramp and resilient container tariffs against a stated fleet-oversupply headwind. Base 50%: H1 FY2026 revenue +13% and stable associate dividends support the central path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum of two parts. The consolidated port business is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream at an 8% HKD WACC, with associate dividends stripped out of the flows. The associate and JV stakes, about half of profit, are valued once in the bridge: SIPG at its quoted price, other listed associates at disclosed market value, and unlisted associates/JVs at 12x normalised earnings (~0.4x their book value). NCI is deducted at its ~28% economic share of the consolidated EV, not at book. Scenario dispersion therefore reflects the consolidated operations only; the associate block is a fixed ~HK$14.7/share in every scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Associate block is fixed across scenarios: every 10% move in the associate stakes (~HK$61.7bn) is ~HK$1.47 per share and is not captured by the bear/bull spread.
Unlisted associates valued at 12x a normalised ~1.45bn share of profit; at the 0.79x of book the listed associates trade on, they would be worth ~HK$16bn more (~HK$3.9/share).

NCI deducted at 28% of base EV (24.6bn) rather than 17.3bn book (~HK$1.7/share higher at book); because it is fixed across scenarios the bear is understated by ~HK$1.9/share and the bull overstated by ~HK$1.5/share versus a proportional NCI charge.

Terminal cap (12x base, 13x bull, 10x bear) binds over Gordon (17x at 8%/2%); finite concession lives (TCP to 2048) argue against higher multiples, and the stock has never traded above 0.92x book at a year-end in FY2017-25.
Scrip-dividend dilution resumed would add non-SBC share growth (count rose 28% FY2017-23).
FX: RMB, BRL, LKR and frontier currencies translate into HKD; the SIPG mark uses CNYHKD 1.1721.

Re-rating dependence: base IV is ~0.95x June-2026 book (HK$27.72/share) and ~16.5x TTM attributable EPS (HK$1.60), against FY2017-25 year-end ranges of 0.39-0.92x book (average 0.56x) and ~5-11x earnings. No-re-rate memo: at the stock's own 0.56x average P/B the value is ~HK$15.5/share, below today's price. The upside in this model is the market's SOE/China holdco discount closing, not faster growth.

no_rerate_memo.basis: FY2017-25 average year-end P/B 0.56x x June-2026 BVPS HK$27.72
no_rerate_memo.note: Memo only, not a replacement for the house value. The gap to the house base (~HK$10.9/share) is the price of the re-rating thesis.

valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: sanity_check.py passed on P/B and P/S only (P/E and EV/EBITDA not evaluated: SBC and EBITDA are NULL in the metrics). A first build with 14x/15x/12x terminal caps implied 1.05x book, above the 10-year maximum; caps were lowered to 12x/13x/10x for finite concession lives before shipping. No post-check fix pass was needed. Final build: implied P/B 1.005x on FY2025 book (0.95x on June-2026 book) against a 0.92x ten-year maximum; check passed.
